To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the virtual certificate paradigm is an efficient and secure way to reduce the size of a certificate chain, thus allowing for faster processing of digital transactions in a PKI-based intercommunity.
virtual certificates and synthetic certificates can be used in order to improve the performance and cost of certificate-based communications in a PKI.

1) virtual and synthetic certificates can be applied to improve the performance and reduce the costs in certificate chains validation, 2) virtual and synthetic certificate chains can be used to reduce the size of certificate chains, 3) virtual certificates can be generated by a Certification Authority, 4) synthetic certificates can be generated at the receiving entity and 5) the generation of virtual certificates can be delegated to a trusted entity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of a new certificate paradigm, which is able to reduce the cost of certificate validation, and therefore, to make more convenient the use of PKIs in e-commerce and e-governance applications.
improving the performance of PKI-based transactions in a large-scale environment, where interoperation among PKI is a common requirement.
new paradigms that can improve the efficiency of the certificate-based validation of public keys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the virtual certificate and synthetic certificates are a very promising solution for improving validation of public key certificates in interoperation of PKIs, which is a problem of high relevance for large organizations.
, although virtual certificates and synthetic certificates are not a substitute for certificates, they can be used to improve the performance of certificate chains.

the proposed virtual and synthetic certificates are a good alternative in order to obtain a better performance of the certificate validation in a PKI, and therefore, of its interoperation with other PKIs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed concepts of virtual certificate, synthetic certificate, and synthetic certificate chain, can be applied to improve the efficiency of validation in a PKI-based network.

the proposed concepts of virtual certificate, synthetic certificate, virtual certificate tree and virtual certificate chain can be used to reduce the number of operations and time required to process a certificate chain, as well as to reduce the amount of data to be processed.
we have proposed a new paradigm for the validation of certificates in a certificate-based network, which is based on the use of virtual and synthetic certificates.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of synthetic certificates and virtual certificates allows to obtain a significant reduction in the processing time and in the cost of validation of certificate chains in inter-community transactions.
the virtual certificate paradigm is a powerful tool to improve the validation of certificate chains, and that synthetic certificates can be used in the context of interoperation among different PKIs.
virtual and synthetic certificates allow to reduce the number of certificates involved in a transaction.
